Marissa — quick data dump below from the week-long sampling run. High level:
- Baseline util (prod fleet): 62% avg across p100/rtx clusters; tail utilization patterns show 18% of time we hit >85% on short windows (10–30 mins).
- Token mix validation: ~72% <64 tokens, ~28% >512 tokens (matches your numbers).
- Incremental burst pricing: estimate $3.40/GPU-hour for T4-equivalent via Apex (ballpark from their doc).

Notes / implications:
- With intelligent KV prefix caching we reduce per-request compute by ~12% on short responses; that translates to ~9% unit cost savings after memory & I/O overheads.
- For the QBR slide I recommend two scenarios: 1) conservative (no burst, aggressive cache tuning) and 2) hybrid (60% reserved + 40% burst during peak windows).

I've attached the short CSV export with slot distribution and sample kernel hotness by sequence length. Irene — can you add kernel-level latency deltas for the short/long splits?

- Karthik

> Marissa — quick data dump below from the week-long sampling run. High level:
> - Baseline util (prod fleet): 62% avg across p100/rtx clusters; tail utilization patterns show 18% of time we hit >85% on short windows (10–30 mins).
> - Token mix validation: ~72% <64 tokens, ~28% >512 tokens (matches your numbers).

I ran an additional kernel routing experiment on the staging lane yesterday. Summary:
- KV cache warm-up dominates the first 45s for short requests if the cache is cold; after warm-up we see a 15-18% reduction in GPU cycles for the same QoR.
- Batching policy A (max latency 120ms) increased effective throughput by ~22% at small QoS cost for long-tail requests.
- Experiment caveat: our single-node quantized kernels show higher variance; need broader sampling for canary.

For the playbook, my recommendation is to:
1) Push cache priming (warm KEYS during off-peak) to reduce cold-start spikes.
2) Apply conservative batching on long-tail with fast-fail fallback to dedicated small-slot pool.
3) Propose a 6-week pilot to validate burst economics (measure tokens-per-GPU-hour with and without burst).

I'll add the latency deltas to Karthik's CSV and tag the kernels in the shared Drive doc.

- Irene
